        self.lhs, self.rhs = exprs

    def resolve_expression(self, query=None, allow_joins=True, reuse=None):
        self.lhs = self.lhs.resolve_expression(query, allow_joins, reuse)

class VarBitField(models.Field):
    description = "A PostgreSQL variable-length bit string."

    def __init__(self, max_length=None, **kwargs):
        if max_length is None:
            raise exceptions.ValidationError("VarBitField requires max_length.")
        self.max_length = int(max_length)
        super().__init__(**kwargs)

    def get_internal_type(self):
        return "VarBitField"

    def db_type(self, connection):
        return f"bit varying({self.max_length})"

    def to_python(self, value):
        if value is None:
            return None
        if isinstance(value, bytes):
            value = value.decode()
        return str(value)

    def get_prep_value(self, value):
        return self.to_python(value)

    def get_db_prep_value(self, value, connection, prepared=False):
        return super().get_db_prep_value(self.get_prep_value(value), connection, prepared=prepared)

    def from_db_value(self, value, expression, connection):
        return self.to_python(value)

IsNull = VarBitField.register_lookup(IsNull)


class BitwiseExpression(Expression):
    def __init__(self, operator, rhs_type, lhs, rhs, output_field=None):
        lhs = F(lhs) if isinstance(lhs, str) else lhs

        self.lhs = lhs

    def set_source_expressions(self, exprs):
        self.lhs, self.rhs = exprs

    def resolve_expression(self, query=None, allow_joins=True, reuse=None):
        self.lhs = self.lhs.resolve_expression(query, allow_joins, reuse)
        self.rhs = self.rhs.resolve_expression(query, allow_joins, reuse)

        return self.as_postgresql(compiler, connection)

        rhs_sql, rhs_params = compiler.compile(self.rhs)
        return f"({lhs_sql} {self.operator} {rhs_sql})", [*lhs_params, *rhs_params]

if(p.t==='puff'){ ctx.fillStyle=`rgba(255,255,255,${(a*.8).toFixed(3)})`; circle(p.x,p.y,p.r*(1.6-a*.6)); } else if(p.t==='dot'){ ctx.fillStyle=`rgba(${p.col},${a.toFixed(3)})`; circle(p.x,p.y,p.r); } else { ctx.save(); ctx.translate(p.x,p.y); ctx.rotate(p.rot); ctx.fillStyle=`rgba(${p.col},${a.toFixed(3)})`; ctx.fillRect(-4,-2.5,8,5); ctx.restore(); } } } function circle(x,y,r){ctx.beginPath();ctx.arc(x,y,r,0,7);ctx.fill();} ``` Game control: ```js function addPipe(x){ const last=pipes[pipes.length-1]; let cy = rnd(GAP_MIN, GAP_MAX); if(last) cy = Math.min(Math.max(cy, last.cy-230), last.cy+230); pipes.push({x: x!==undefined?x:W+30, cy, scored:false}); } function reset(){ bird.y=300; bird.vy=0; bird.rot=0; pipes=[]; parts=[]; score=0; newBest=false; flash=0; shake=0; popT=1; addPipe(W+60); spawnAcc=0; } function startPlay(){ reset(); state=ST.PLAY; flap(); } function flap(){ bird.vy=FLAP; wingBoost=1; puff(); Sfx.flap(); } function hit(){ state=ST.DYING; flash=1; shake=13; bird.vy=-180; Sfx.hit(); Sfx.die(); burst(); } function land(){ bird.y=GROUND-BIRD_R; state=ST.OVER; overAt=performance.now(); panelT=0; if(score>best){best=score;newBest=true;try{localStorage.setItem('flappy.best',String(best))}catch(e){}} Sfx.land(); dust(); } ``` Update: ```js function update(dt){ simT+=dt; flash=Math.max(0,flash-dt*2.4); shake=Math.max(0,shake-dt*42); popT=Math.min(1,popT+dt*3.2); wingBoost=Math.max(0,wingBoost-dt*3); if(state===ST.PAUSE) return; wingPhase+=dt*(state===ST.PLAY?13:state===ST.DYING?3:6); updateParts(dt); // clouds for(const c of clouds){ c.x-=(state===ST.PLAY? c.v*2.2 : c.v*0.8)*dt*? ``` Wait, cloud speed: c.v px/s base 6-10. In PLAY double for parallax feel? Actually clouds are background, slowest parallax; keep it simple: c.x -= c.v*dt*(state===ST.PLAY?1.6:0.7). Fine. ``` if(c.x<-90){ c.x=W+90; c.y=Math.min(430,Math.max(60,c.y+rnd(-50,50))); } } if(state===ST.READY){ worldDist+=80*dt; bird.y=300+Math.sin(simT*2.6)*9; bird.rot=Math.sin(simT*2.6+1.2)*0.07; } else if(state===ST.PLAY){ worldDist+=SPEED*dt; bird.vy=Math.min(bird.vy+GRAV*dt,VMAX); bird.y+=bird.vy*dt; if(bird.y<-70){bird.y=-70; if(bird.vy<0)bird.vy=0;} // rotation const target = bird.vy<0 ? -0.38 : Math.min(1.5,(bird.vy/520)*1.5); bird.rot += (target-bird.rot)*Math.min(1,dt*(bird.vy<0?16:7)); // pipes for(const p of pipes) p.x-=SPEED*dt; if(pipes.length && pipes[0].x<-PIPE_W-10) pipes.shift(); spawnAcc+=SPEED*dt; if(spawnAcc>=SPACING){ spawnAcc-=SPACING; addPipe(); } // scoring for(const p of pipes) if(!p.scored && p.x+PIPE_W=GROUND){ bird.y=GROUND-BIRD_R; hit(); } else for(const p of pipes){ const top=p.cy-GAP/2, bot=p.cy+GAP/2; if( circleRect(bird.x,bird.y,BIRD_R,p.x,-300,PIPE_W,top+300) || circleRect(bird.x,bird.y,BIRD_R,p.x,bot,PIPE_W,GROUND-bot) || circleRect(bird.x,bird.y,BIRD_R,p.x-5,top-26,PIPE_W+10,26) || circleRect(bird.x,bird.y,BIRD_R,p.x-5,bot,PIPE_W+10,26) ){ hit(); break; } } } else if(state===ST.DYING){ bird.vy=Math.min(bird.vy+GRAV*dt,VMAX); bird.y+=bird.vy*dt; bird.rot += (1.55-bird.rot)*Math.min(1,dt*10); if(bird.y+BIRD_R>=GROUND) land(); } else if(state===ST.OVER){ panelT=Math.min(1,panelT+dt*3); } } ``` Render: ```js function render(){ const sx=(Math.random()*2-1)*shake, sy=(Math.random()*2-1)*shake; ctx.save(); ctx.translate(sx,sy); drawSky(); // clouds for(const c of clouds) drawCloud(c); drawHills(); drawPipes(); drawGround(); drawBird(); drawParts(); if(state===ST.READY) drawStart(); if(state===ST.OVER) drawOver(); if(state===ST.PAUSE) drawPause(); if(state!==ST.READY) drawScore(); ctx.restore(); if(flash>0){ ctx.fillStyle=`rgba(255,255,255,${(flash*.75).toFixed(3)})`; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H); } } ``` Shake with random each frame is fine. drawSky: ```js function drawSky(){ const g=ctx.createLinearGradient(0,0,0,GROUND); g.addColorStop(0,'#5ec3d7'); g.addColorStop(.55,'#7fd4dd'); g.addColorStop(1,'#c6ecdf'); ctx.fillStyle=g; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H); // sun ctx.fillStyle='rgba(255,250,214,.35)'; circle(338,92,52); ctx.fillStyle='#fff6cf'; circle(338,92,34); } ``` Sky blue #5ec3d7 top... spec "blue sky" ✓. drawCloud(c): ```js function drawCloud(c){ const s=c.s; ctx.save(); ctx.translate(c.x,c.y); ctx.scale(s,s); ctx.fillStyle='rgba(255,255,255,.88)'; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(-20,2,13,0,7); ctx.arc(0,-8,17,0,7); ctx.arc(20,2,12,0,7); ctx.arc(2,-2,14,0,7); ctx.fill(); ctx.restore(); } ``` Union of arcs with default nonzero fill → puffy. Flat bottom? add fillRect(-30,2,60,8)? Then it looks slabby; skip. drawHills: ```js function bumpRow(baseY,step,h,off,fill){ ctx.fillStyle=fill; ctx.beginPath(); const o=off%step; for(let x=-o-step; x0){ rr(150,498,120,34,17); ctx.fillStyle='rgba(7,34,42,.18)'; ctx.fill(); pxText('BEST',180,516,9,'rgba(12,50,60,.75)',0); pxText(String(best),232,516,11,'#ffffff',4); } } ``` Hmm, pill with BEST: two texts 'BEST' and value in pill width 120: BEST (4 chars ×9px ≈ 36+? Press Start 2P 9px char width ≈ 9px → BEST=36, value 2 digits 22). Position: BEST at 180 center, value 232. ok. Actually stroke 0 means no stroke; pxText signature (txt,x,y,size,fill,stroke,strokeCol...) stroke 0 → skip stroke. Good. Bird at y≈300 in READY, title 148-196 above, pill 410 below. Bird between. drawScore: ```js function drawScore(){ const s=1+0.32*Math.sin(popT*Math.PI); ctx.save(); ctx.translate(210,62); ctx.scale(s,s); pxText(String(score),0,0,30,'#ffffff',8); ctx.restore(); } ``` When popT=1 (idle), sin(π)=0 → s=1 ✓. drawOver: ```js function drawOver(){ const e=1-Math.pow(1-panelT,3); // easeOutCubic ctx.fillStyle=`rgba(7,30,38,${(0.45*e).toFixed(3)})`; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H); const oy=(1-e)*-24; // header pxText('GAME OVER',210,140+oy,22,'#ff9040',7,'rgba(7,30,38,.95)'); // panel ctx.save(); ctx.globalAlpha=e; ctx.translate(0,oy); rr(58,186,304,216,16); ctx.fillStyle='#f6e6c3'; ctx.fill(); ctx.lineWidth=4; ctx.strokeStyle='#b98a4e'; rr(58,186,304,216,16); ctx.stroke(); rr(64,192,292,204,12); ctx.strokeStyle='rgba(255,255,255,.55)'; ctx.lineWidth=2; ctx.stroke(); // divider ctx.strokeStyle='rgba(0,0,0,.10)'; ctx.lineWidth=2; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(196,220); ctx.lineTo(196,368); ctx.stroke(); // medal const m = score>=40?4:score>=30?3:score>=20?2:score>=10?1:0; const medalCols=[null,['#a56a2f','#d99a55'],['#9aa4ad','#cdd6dd'],['#d49a1e','#ffd450'],['#7fc7cf','#c9f0f4']]; const mcx=126,mcy=292; if(m===0){ ctx.setLineDash([5,5]); ctx.strokeStyle='rgba(90,70,40,.35)'; ctx.lineWidth=3; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(mcx,mcy,34,0,7); ctx.stroke(); ctx.setLineDash([]); uiText('?',mcx,mcy+2,30,'rgba(90,70,40,.5)',900); } else { const [d,l]=medalCols[m]; ctx.fillStyle=d; circle(mcx,mcy,36); ctx.fillStyle=l; circle(mcx,mcy,29); ctx.strokeStyle='rgba(255,255,255,.5)'; ctx.lineWidth=3; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(mcx,mcy,31.5,-2.6,-1.1); ctx.stroke(); star(mcx,mcy,12,'rgba(120,80,20,.35)'); } pxText('MEDAL',mcx,352,9,'#8a6a3f',0); // right scores pxText('SCORE',268,238,10,'#8a6a3f',0); pxText(String(score),268,268,26,'#33261a'? ... ``` Hmm, value color: use dark brown '#4a3419' fill, no stroke: pxText(String(score),268,266,24,'#4a3419',0). BEST: pxText('BEST',268,318,10,'#8a6a3f',0); pxText(String(best),268,346,24, newBest? '#c2452e' : '#4a3419',0). NEW badge if newBest: save rotate(-0.1) at (332,326)? Place near top right of panel: ``` if(newBest){ ctx.save(); ctx.translate(330,232); ctx.rotate(-.09); rr(-32,-13,64,26,13); ctx.fillStyle='#e8564a'; ctx.fill(); pxText('NEW!',0,1,9,'#fff',0); ctx.restore(); } ``` Panel x 58..362, y 186..402. NEW at (330,232) inside ✓. But SCORE label at y238 x268 — badge may overlap; shift badge to y=214? rr(-32,-13): covers y 201..227 at x 298..362 — inside panel top-right, above SCORE label (238). ok good. ``` ctx.restore(); // panel alpha // retry hint const bl=0.5+0.5*Math.sin(simT*4); pxText('TAP / SPACE TO RETRY',210,448,9,`rgba(255,255,255,${(0.35+0.6*bl).toFixed(2)})`,5,'rgba(7,30,38,.9)'); } ``` Wait, globalAlpha panel restore — after restore hint is full alpha, fine. Header 'GAME OVER' at 140; panel top 186 → overlap ok. Bird lying on ground at left; panel covers center; fine. drawPause: ```js function drawPause(){ ctx.fillStyle='rgba(7,30,38,.5)'; ctx.fillRect(0,0,W,H); pxText('PAUSED',210,290,24,'#ffffff',7); uiText('tap or press P to resume',210,330,15,'rgba(255,255,255,.8)',800); } ``` star(): ```js function star(cx,cy,r,col){ ctx.fillStyle=col; ctx.beginPath(); for(let i=0;i<5;i++){ const a=-Math.PI/2+i*2*Math.PI/5; const a2=a+Math.PI/5; ctx.lineTo(cx+Math.cos(a)*r, cy+Math.sin(a)*r); ctx.lineTo(cx+Math.cos(a2)*r*.45, cy+Math.sin(a2)*r*.45); } ctx.closePath(); ctx.fill(); } ``` Main loop: ```js let last=performance.now(); function loop(now){ requestAnimationFrame(loop); let dt=(now-last)/1000; last=now; if(!(dt>0)) dt=0; dt=Math.min(dt,0.033); update(dt); render(); } requestAnimationFrame(loop); ``` First frame dt: now vs last set at load → small. Fine. Input: ```js function primary(){ Sfx.unlock(); if(state===ST.READY) startPlay(); else if(state===ST.PLAY) flap(); else if(state===ST.PAUSE) state=ST.PLAY; else if(state===ST.OVER){ if(performance.now()-overAt>450) startPlay(); } } canvas.addEventListener('pointerdown', e=>{ e.preventDefault(); primary(); }); window.addEventListener('keydown', e=>{ if(e.code==='Space'||e.code==='ArrowUp'){ e.preventDefault(); if(!e.repeat) primary(); } else if(e.code==='KeyP'){ if(state===ST.PLAY) state=ST.PAUSE; else if(state===ST.PAUSE) state=ST.PLAY; } else if(e.code==='KeyM'){ toggleMute(); } }); document.addEventListener('visibilitychange',()=>{ if(document.hidden && state===ST.PLAY) state=ST.PAUSE; }); window.addEventListener('blur',()=>{ if(state===ST.PLAY) state=ST.PAUSE; }); ``` Note: pointerdown on canvas only; but keydown Space is window. If user hovers over mute button and presses space, it will flap — acceptable. But wait: if we press M with focus on mute button, does the button also receive keydown? Space would click the button if it has focus → also flap: e.preventDefault prevents default button activation? Space on focused button fires click on keyup by default; preventDefault on keydown prevents it. We preventDefault Space globally ✓. Enter would click mute — no Enter handling, fine. fit(): ```js function fit(){ const top=document.querySelector('.cab-top'), bot=document.querySelector('.cab-bottom'); const chrome=(top?top.offsetHeight:40)+(bot?bot.offsetHeight:34)+34; // paddings const availH=window.innerHeight-chrome-20; const availW=window.innerWidth-36; const s=Math.max(.35,Math.min(1,availW/W,availH/H)); canvas.style.width=Math.round(W*s)+'px'; } window.addEventListener('resize',fit); fit(); ``` Note: canvas.style.width overrides CSS width:420px. If s=1, 420. height auto keeps ratio. Also, if screen is extremely short, s<1 shrinks. Good. Sfx object definition order: muted referenced in Sfx — declare `let muted` before Sfx. toggleMute defined after; used in keydown — function declarations hoist ✓. Final Sfx: ```js const Sfx=(()=>{ let c=null; const ok=()=>{ if(!c){ try{ c=new (window.AudioContext||window.webkitAudioContext)(); }catch(e){} } if(c&&c.state==='suspended') c.resume(); return c; }; function tone(f0,f1,t,type,v,when=0){ const a=ok(); if(!a||muted)return; const o=a.createOscillator(), g=a.createGain(), n=a.currentTime+when; o.type=type; o.frequency.setValueAtTime(Math.max(30,f0),n); if(f1) o.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(30,f1),n+t); g.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001,n); g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(v,n+0.012); g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001,n+t); o.connect(g).connect(a.destination); o.start(n); o.stop(n+t+0.06); } function noise(t,v,when=0,f=900){ const a=ok(); if(!a||muted)return; const n=Math.floor(a.sampleRate*t), buf=a.createBuffer(1,n,a.sampleRate), d=buf.getChannelData(0); for(let i=0;i0 ✓. Brand svg: ```html ``` Rough pixel bird. Fine. Title tag, noscript inside screen? add

messages.content:
Create an HTML5 single page application that mimics Slack

## Requirements

- Use HTML5 Canvas for rendering
- Emojis must be prominent and easy as menus on posted messages
- Messages must be displayed in a chat-like interface
- Channels must be displayed in a sidebar
- Users must be displayed in a sidebar
- Typing `:` must trigger emoji picker
- Avatars must be displayed in the chat interface
- A control setting must be available to set the number of simulated users who post messages so the interface feels lively.
- Simulated users must not spam messages, they must post messages at random intervals that resembles typing based on natural delays and typing speed.
- The interface must be responsive and work on different screen sizes.
- The interface must be visually appealing and modern.
- The interface must be easy to use and navigate.
- The interface must be accessible and work on different browsers.
- Sending a message must provide an animation of the message leaving the input field and appearing in the chat.

results.reasoning_content: Let's build a comprehensive HTML5 canvas-based Slack clone as a single-page application. This is a big project. Main requirements: 1. Use HTML5 canvas for rendering 2. Make emojis prominent, easy to use as a menu on posted messages (e.g., reaction button on hover / clicking the message shows an emoji reaction menu) 3. Chat-like message interface 4. Channels in a sidebar 5. Users in a sidebar 6. Typing `:` triggers the emoji picker 7. Avatars in the chat 8. A control to set how many simulated users post messages 9. Simulated users post at random intervals that look like typing (natural delays, typing speed) 10. Responsive 11. Visually attractive and modern 12. Easy to use 13. Accessible across browsers 14. Animation of message leaving the input field and appearing in the chat Design considerations: - Rather than defaulting to a center-aligned hero, start with what's most characteristic of the subject — this is a Slack clone, so start directly with the app UI (workspace bar, sidebars, chat). - Use a distinctive display typeface + a readable body typeface. Since it's an app, maybe we can use Google Fonts... but a single file? We can use a Google Fonts link (webfont) — a single HTML file can load fonts from a CDN. "Work on different browsers" — web fonts should be fine with fallbacks. Let's pick a display face like "Sora" or "Outfit" for headings/brand, and a readable body face like "Public Sans", or... Slack itself uses Lato. Let's use "Bricolage Grotesque" or "Sora" for display, and "Atkinson Hyperlegible" for body? Atkinson Hyperlegible is great for accessibility. Or "IBM Plex Sans". Let's go with this: - Display: "Sora" (700/800) for the workspace name, section headers, maybe for big numbers too. - Body: "Atkinson Hyperlegible" — very readable and accessible. Hmm, but for chat messages maybe "IBM Plex Sans" would be better. Actually, let's use "Sora" + "IBM Plex Sans" — Plex Sans is very readable and has many weights. Or Space Grotesk + Inter? No, let's avoid Inter; use "Public Sans" or "IBM Plex Sans". Decision: display "Sora", body "IBM Plex Sans". Fallback is system fonts. For canvas rendering, after font loading (document.fonts.ready), we need to use a font stack that canvas can use: `13px "IBM Plex Sans", system-ui, sans-serif`. - Color: Slack-like but not a copy — a dark sidebar with a distinctive palette. Slack uses aubergine #4A154B. Should we make our own? Teal / deep green ("evergreen" #1f2937?). Let's make something unique: a deep "ink blue" sidebar? Hmm, the subject is characteristic — Slack is known for its aubergine. We can do a deep plum aubergine with a modern twist and vivid accent. Let's design a palette: - Base background: soft off-white #f6f4f0? The page is a full app, so the app chrome is: - Left rail (workspace column): deep aubergine `#3b1f3f` / `#46214d`? Or something more modern: deep forest `#0f2e26`? Hmm. - Let's pick: rail `#2a1626` (deep plum), sidebar `#3a2140`... actually, Slack-style two-tone: rail #35113a? Let's build: - `--ink: #2b1b33` (deep plum) rail - `--panel: #372242`? Maybe too purple. Alternative: deep teal + warm accent. - Chat background: `#faf8f5` warm light. Accent: "coral"? Slack accent is blue #116466. Let's commit to a palette: - Rail: `#241a2e` (very dark plum) - Sidebar: `#2f2138` - Sidebar hover: `#42304f` - Active channel: `#5a3f6b`? Or accent fill with light text. - Chat background: `#fbfaf7` (warm paper) - Text: `#241a2e` - Accent: `#7c5cff`? That's a purple / indigo gradient vibe... let's avoid. Warm amber / orange accent `#ff5c38`? Or teal `#0d9488`? A lively Slack-esque feel: accent coral `#f0533d`? Hmm, message animation "leaving the input" — accent color for my own messages. - My identity accent: `#1f8a70`? Let's make "me" teal and the bot accent coral. Actually, a strong choice: aubergine chrome + cream chat + "electric chartreuse"? No. Let's go with plum + cream + coral (#ff5a3c) + teal secondary. This is a lively, warm, distinctive palette that isn't black and beige. Good. - Layout: - Top bar (workspace): name "Ember Slack"? Let's call it a fake company "Lumen & Co." or "Nimbus". Canvas-drawn top bar: workspace name with logo, search field, settings gear, my avatar. - Left rail: workspace switch, channels icon, DM icon, settings/control icon (opens the control panel for sim user count). - Sidebar: "Channels" list with # icon and unread badges; "Direct messages" or a user list with presence dots (online/away/dnd); user list. - Main chat: channel header (channel name, topic, member count), message list, typing indicator, composer. - Right side (optional): member details? Could add on wide screens. Since it's all canvas, we need a full custom layout engine with hit testing, scroll regions, hover states, keyboard navigation, accessibility (canvas a11y is tricky — provide aria-live region and sr-only text updates, focus handling, and a fallback description). Accessibility: canvas can't be focused per element; what to add: - An offscreen `aria-live="polite"` region that announces new messages. - `role="application"` on the canvas with an aria-label describing the app. - Keyboard: Enter to send, arrows to move through channel list, `:` for emoji, Esc to close menus. - Provide a visible focus ring on the currently "focused" canvas widget. - prefers-reduced-motion: reduce animations. - Rendering approach: A single canvas that fills the window, devicePixelRatio-scaled. A scene graph of rectangles/zones with pointer handlers. A game loop with requestAnimationFrame that renders each frame (or re-render on dirty; simpler: render every frame — should be fine with a moderate message count; still, re-rendering text every frame with many lines could get heavy. Messages can have pre-rendered offscreen canvases? Simpler: keep the total messages reasonable (cap at ~150), batch text and render every frame. Modern browsers should handle this fine. But to be safe, implement dirty rendering + a render queue: rAF only renders when needed, or when animations are active. Animations (typing indicator, message entrance, presence dots, clock) suggest continuous animation... a clock that updates every second triggers re-render — that's fine. Keep continuous rAF but cache message layout (text lines computed once, stored). Each frame only does fillText for visible lines — with ~40 visible lines that's fine. - Emoji handling: - Shortcode parser: map `:wave:`, `:rocket:` etc. to Unicode emoji when rendering; canvas text handles most emoji well (color emoji). Provide a map of about 60–100 shortcodes. - Composer input: `:` triggers emoji picker (a small search box, grid). Since it's canvas, do we need an actual hidden `` for the text? Hmm — the requirement is to use HTML5 canvas for rendering. Typing: we can capture keydown on document and manage the text string ourselves, rendering the composer text on canvas, with a fake caret. It avoids native input styling issues and keeps everything on canvas. But accessibility: a hidden native input is better for screen readers... we can use a visually-hidden native input that is programmatically focused to capture IME/typing and aria-live? Simpler and more robust approach: use a visually hidden real `` (opacity 0, positioned over the composer or offscreen but focusable) that captures keyboard input (including paste, IME), and mirror the value into the canvas rendering. This gives real accessibility (screen reader reads the input), real caret? The native caret isn't visible, but we can draw our own caret synced with value length. This is a solid hybrid: canvas rendering + native input semantics. - Emojis in message text: convert shortcodes to emoji at render time; when rendering mixed text with emoji, use ctx.fillText on the full string — color emojis render fine on canvas on most browsers. Good. - Prominent emoji menu on posted messages: on hover (or click) over a message, show a floating action bar with ~8 prominent emoji buttons (larger, e.g., 👍 ❤️ 😂 🎉 👀 🚀 💯) + a "+ 😀" that opens the full emoji picker to add a reaction. Also click on the message itself (or reaction pill) to toggle reactions. Reaction pills show emoji + count and highlight when the user has reacted. This satisfies "make emojis prominent, easy to use as a menu on posted messages." - Simulated users: - A pool of ~12 named users with avatar colors, presence, and persona (e.g., designer, dev, PM) that generate on-topic messages per channel. - Control: a "simulation" panel with a slider / stepper for the number of active simulated users (0–12), plus maybe a "pace" control? The requirement says "a control to set the number of simulated users who post messages." What to add: a stepper / slider 0..12, and maybe a pause toggle. Place under a gear in the rail or under "Automation" in the sidebar. Let's make a canvas panel that opens from the rail icon: "Live simulation" with slider + preset chips (Quiet/Lively/Busy) + per-user toggles? Let's keep it: a count slider, and a small list of the active users with toggles. Keep it manageable: a count slider + presence chips. - Natural typing: each simulated user picks the next message after a random idle (e.g., 4–30 seconds depending on the user). When posting, show a typing indicator in the channel ("Riley is typing…"), the duration is proportional to message length / typing speed (wpm 40–90), with small pauses; then post the message with an entrance animation. Avoid spam: enforce a minimum interval, and when the count is high, scale intervals. Typing indicator shows up in the channel where they post. The message only appears after the typing finishes. - Messages sometimes reference others, sometimes include emoji shortcodes, and occasionally add reactions to recent messages (bots react to each other / to your messages) — fun touch: when the user sends a message, a few bots might react or reply ("Nice!", "👀"). - Channels: e.g., # general, # design, # engineering, # random, # announcements. Unread badge updates when a bot posts to a channel you're not viewing. Click to switch channel, scroll to bottom. - Users sidebar: presence dot (online green, away amber, dnd red / do not disturb ring), name, status message ("In a meeting 🎧"), list with small avatar. Also show "X people online". DM section? The requirement says to show users in the sidebar — presence list. Add a DM section with a few users; clicking a user opens a DM channel (messages are simulated there too? Simpler: DMs show a simulated 1-on-1 conversation; a simulated user may reply when you send). Feasible: give DMs a light simulation where the other user sometimes replies. Keep the scope sane.
